title: CORS allows any origin together with credentials
description: CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins=["*"] and allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject the wildcard-with-credentials combination per the fetch spec, but some clients/proxies do not enforce this, and the intent (any origin, with cookies/Authorization headers allowed) is itself unsafe for an authenticated API.
impact: If enforced loosely by a client or a future same-site cookie is introduced, any website could make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of a logged-in user, enabling CSRF-style data theft against /projects, /sessions, /analytics.

title: Hardcoded fallback JWT secret key
description: SECRET_KEY defaults to the literal string "ccm-tracker-dev-secret-change-me" whenever TRACKER_SECRET_KEY is not set in the environment. This default is committed to the repo and predictable.
impact: If the app is ever run without TRACKER_SECRET_KEY set (e.g. a misconfigured deployment), anyone who has read this file can forge valid access and refresh tokens for any user id, fully bypassing authentication.

title: Unhandled ValueError when JWT subject is not numeric
description: get_current_user reads user_id = payload.get("sub") inside a try/except JWTError block, but int(user_id) is called later, outside that try block, in the db.query(...) filter. If a token's "sub" claim is not an integer-parseable string, int() raises ValueError which is not caught anywhere.
impact: A malformed or tampered token (or any future bug that puts a non-numeric subject into a token) causes an unhandled 500 Internal Server Error instead of a clean 401, and can leak a stack trace if the app is run with debug/reload output visible.

title: OAuth2PasswordBearer tokenUrl does not match the login endpoint's request format
description: auth.py declares oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="/auth/login"), which tells FastAPI's interactive docs to POST form-encoded username/password to that URL. The actual /auth/login route (app/routers/auth.py:46) expects a JSON body matching the LoginIn model, not form data.
impact: The "Authorize" button in /docs (Swagger UI) will fail to log in, since it submits OAuth2 form data instead of JSON — breaking the exact 'hit /docs' verification workflow described in the project's CLAUDE.md.

title: TOCTOU race condition on username/email uniqueness checks
description: register() checks for existing username and email with separate SELECT queries, then inserts a new row. Two concurrent requests with the same username/email can both pass the checks before either commits, since there is no transaction-level locking and the checks are not atomic with the insert.
impact: Concurrent duplicate registrations can raise an unhandled IntegrityError from the unique constraint on commit, returning a 500 instead of the intended 400 'already registered' response.

title: Refresh tokens are issued but never usable or revocable
description: create_refresh_token() generates a refresh token with a jti claim and 7-day expiry, and /auth/login returns it to the client (app/routers/auth.py:52). However, there is no /auth/refresh route to redeem a refresh token for a new access token, and the jti is never persisted, so it can't be checked or revoked either.
impact: The refresh-token feature is dead/incomplete: clients receive a token they cannot use, and if the intent is later completed naively (e.g. accept any unexpired refresh token), there is no revocation mechanism for compromised tokens.

title: get_current_active_user is dead code and its error path is unreachable
description: get_current_user's own DB query already filters models.User.is_active == True (auth.py:61), so an inactive user is filtered out and get_current_user raises 'Invalid or expired token' (401) before get_current_active_user's explicit 'Inactive user' (400) check can ever run. No router actually depends on get_current_active_user anyway.
impact: Dead code adds maintenance confusion, and inactive/deactivated users receive a misleading 401 'invalid token' error rather than a clear 400 'inactive user' message.

title: No password strength or minimum length validation on registration
description: RegisterIn.password is typed as a plain str with no min_length, complexity, or max_length constraint, so empty or single-character passwords are accepted by /auth/register.
impact: Weak passwords are permitted, making accounts easier to brute-force; combined with no login rate limiting (finding 11), this materially weakens account security.

title: List endpoints have no pagination
description: list_projects (app/routers/projects.py:42-52) and list_sessions (app/routers/sessions.py:59-68) return all matching rows for a user with no limit/offset or page size cap.
impact: A user (or account) with a large number of projects or session logs will receive an unbounded response payload, increasing latency and memory use as data grows.

title: bcrypt silently truncates passwords beyond 72 bytes
description: pwd_context uses the bcrypt scheme directly with no pre-hashing step. bcrypt only considers the first 72 bytes of input, so passwords longer than that are truncated before hashing with no warning to the user.
impact: Users who choose long passphrases believe their full password is protecting the account, but only the first 72 bytes actually matter, silently reducing effective password strength for those users.

title: No rate limiting or lockout on login
description: The /auth/login route has no throttling, attempt counting, or lockout logic; verify_password is called for every request with no delay or backoff.
impact: The endpoint is vulnerable to online brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against user passwords, especially combined with the lack of a minimum password length (finding 8).

title: Static frontend directory is mounted without an existence check
description: app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=FRONTEND_DIR), ...) and the root() handler's FileResponse(FRONTEND_DIR / "index.html") both assume app/frontend exists with an index.html, with no check or fallback if the directory or file is missing.
impact: If the frontend directory is absent or misnamed in a given checkout/deployment, the app fails at import/startup time (StaticFiles raises if the directory doesn't exist) or the root route returns a raw file-not-found error instead of a clear diagnostic.
